reviews.text: Hyperliquid is a decentralized perpetuals exchange built on its own layer-1 blockchain, specializing in high-leverage trading with zero gas fees for orders. Launched in 2023, it gained popularity for its liquid staking and fast execution, attracting traders from centralized platforms. The team is anonymous but has delivered consistent updates. In 2025, it expanded to include spot markets, but regulatory scrutiny on perps is increasing. It’s a solid option for advanced traders, though not beginner-friendly.

Hyperliqud is an EVM-based blockchain running on the Hyperliquid network, which has its own L1. Also its a Perp Dex . Perp Dex is also called Hyperliquid. The currency name is hype. I think it is a perp dex that will be very, very powerful with future regulations.

Hyperliquid is a perpetual trading protocol developed on its own Layer-1 blockchain. At the moment it is the market leader.
Hyperliquid wants to deliver a CEX like user experience but onchain. Backed by a small team (no VCs), it achieved over 2.7B$ TVL and over 20B$ in perpetual trading during its peak in September.
Its blockchain, an L1 (HyperEVM), can handle ~200k TPS with ~0.2s latency.
Features include “Pre-Markets” auctions for trading tokens before launch, vaults that can auto-copy profitable traders. It is famous also thanks to the token airdrop that included a huge audience of people. Recent innovations include HIP-3 (giving the possibility to everyone to create a perpetual platform) and USDH stablecoin backed by US treasuries in partnership with BlackRock and Stripe.

The project presents a platform that is DeFI oriented, operating as a layer 1 (L1) platform, it seeks to present a better platform that is more enhanced and makes for an easier operation. You could either start trading or start building on the platform. It uses a custom consensus algorithm called HyperBFT, just as HyperEVM was equally adopted.

Hyperliquid is an open source, EVM compatible Layer 1 blockchain that focuses on DeFi and user experience which gave rise to its in-built DEX. The protocol uses Hyper Byzantine Fault Tolerance (HyperBFT) consensus mechanism which gives it a high speed. The core contributors of Hyperliquid are professionals from Harvard and they maintained the idea of self funding to avoid any VC funding to avoid being controlled by the VCs. However, the treasury of HYPE tokens managed by Hyperliquid Strategies Inc. (HSI), a publicly listed entity that has a huge amount of investment from Panthera capitals. In my opinion Hyperliquid has a good potential.

Hyperliquid strikes me as a powerful trading platform built on its own blockchain. It seems tailored for serious perpetual traders, and I admire its low fees and high throughput. Still, I can’t help but wonder if most users will switch to such a new exchange when big players already exist.

After checking Hyperliquid, my honest take is that it’s a strong trading platform, mainly for people who love perps and fast execution. It feels quick and simple to use, and many traders seem to like it. But at the same time, some things don’t feel very clear to me, especially around decentralization and how much control the team really has. It’s good for active traders, but I still think the project carries some risks.
